wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran, a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are trying to understand the country at a given moment rather than any measure of Iran itself.
wiki-iran.recent: The peak on Aug 25 came as Treasury Secretary Bessent's "Operation Economic Outcast" widened sanctions to nearly 60 entities and bound third-country banks, and as Trump declared Hormuz clear while Iran and Oman charted only a temporary corridor. Pezeshkian has since conceded foreign trade has shrunk by more than a third.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Brent fell about a tenth over the window despite the Strait of Hormuz, which carries a fifth of the world's oil, thinning to a single gas carrier on Monday. Inventory absorbed the closure before price did: China cut oil imports 45%, and Washington declared the strait open on Thursday with 7 tankers crossing.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered in Cushing, Oklahoma — the benchmark for oil produced in the United States. It sets what American refiners pay, and petrol, diesel and freight costs follow it.
wti.recent: Prices have fallen back from the August spike that took oil above $91 after Trump signalled he would not renew the Iran deal. The retreat held even as Hormuz traffic fell to single digits, because China cut oil imports 45% and inventories absorbed the chokepoint before the price did.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline junction and used to price most American gas contracts. It sets what power stations, chemical plants and heating bills cost, and it anchors the price of LNG loaded for export.
natgas-hh.recent: The 60-day slide to $2.70 is a US story, but the export-linked market moved the other way: LNG prices surged after the escalation in West Asia, pushing Delhi's compressed natural gas up ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg, while Pakistan apologized for night-time blackouts after an RLNG cargo delay. Iran reported a Fars gas find of 161 billion cubic meters.

wheat.standing: The world reference price for milling wheat, quoted per tonne. It sets the cost of bread, flour and animal feed across import-dependent economies, and governments that subsidise or stockpile grain budget against it.
wheat.recent: The series ran from $155.1/mt in Sep 2025 to $228.7/mt in Jul 2026, a 30% rise. Sindh's decision to import 5 million tons of wheat after withdrawing its support price points to the import demand behind the climb, and buyers in Africa have been shifting toward cassava and sorghum flour.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple grain for roughly half the planet and the one whose cost is felt fastest in Asian and West African household budgets. It moves on monsoon rains, harvests and export bans, and food-price inflation follows it.
rice.recent: The price has fallen 17.7% over the series, to $464 per tonne from a high of $563.8 in Aug 2024 and off a low of $330.6 in Oct 2025. The input does not name a cause for the move.

copper.standing: The price of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity in every cable, motor and transformer. Demand for it tracks building, wiring and grid construction, which is why it is read as a gauge of industrial activity.
copper.recent: The series sits near its high of 13,550 $/mt in Jun 2026, roughly half again above the Dec 2024 low of 8,910. Copper demand is being pulled by electrification: grid hardware is under strain from EV charging, transformer designs are being reworked for AI-driven load, and Washington has banned foreign grid parts. Zambia reelected Hakainde Hichilema, whose copper revenues underpin its debt restructuring.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, and the reference rate for long-term borrowing worldwide. Mortgages, corporate loans and emerging-market debt are all priced off it, so when it moves, the cost of money moves everywhere.
us-10y.recent: Yields rose across the curve into late August, with the thirty-year reaching 5.3%, a level last seen in 2007. Traders spent the week positioning around Warsh's Jackson Hole speech and what his tone would say about Fed independence, while Bessent's "Economic Outcast" sanctions campaign against Iran added a second source of pressure.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies, and the default measure of American equity performance. Trillions in pension and index funds track it, so a company's admission to it forces buying by funds that must hold whatever it holds.
sp500.recent: The index sits near its Aug 13 high after a run driven by AI capital spending and unsettled by rates. Nvidia pledged $500 billion to finance its own buyers, while Fed minutes showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed and Treasury yields rose on strong services data. Reddit jumped 11% on an index committee's decision alone.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. Concentrated in chipmakers and platforms, it is the cleanest read on how much the market will pay for the technology trade.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits below its early-June high despite Nvidia beating expectations and guiding to $108bn in revenue for the next quarter — a beat that did not settle the questions around it, since Nvidia also backstops $230 billion in customer lease obligations and pledged $500 billion to its own buyers.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump, surveyed weekly across the country. It follows crude, but refining capacity and taxes sit between the two, and it is the price most households feel first when either moves.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refining, not crude, has been the constraint: Ukrainian drones struck the Samara refinery on 22 August, Moscow capped station sales at 30 litres, and Putin conceded that "not all fuel issues have been resolved" while Novak said Russia would import fuel and lower standards. US pump prices still eased, down about 5% over the window.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of gas at the Dutch TTF hub, Europe's benchmark for pipeline and imported LNG. Because Europe now buys much of its gas on the seaborne spot market, it competes with Asian buyers, and heating, power and fertiliser costs follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: The rise runs through LNG. Indraprastha Gas raised Delhi CNG by ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg on 29 August, citing surging global LNG prices amid the West Asia crisis — the same spot market Europe buys from, with Hormuz shipping the constraint. Iran's Fars discovery of 161 billion cubic meters is reserves, not near-term supply.

vix.standing: The Cboe index of expected volatility in the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from what traders pay for options. It rises when investors buy protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of fear in American equities.
vix.recent: Volatility has drained steadily out of the market since early summer. The index peaked at 22.22 on Jun 10, fell to a low of 14.25 on Aug 14, and has settled at 14.51 — a quiet reading by its own standards.

fx-pkr.standing: The Pakistani rupee against the US dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel, machinery and often its wheat, so the rate sets the cost of the import bill and the burden of dollar-denominated debt on the state's budget.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee held in a narrow band, near 277.6 to the dollar. The pressures on it are the import side: Pakistan is buying 5 million tons of wheat for Sindh, an RLNG cargo delay left the grid short and forced night-time blackouts, and oil marketing companies keep building fuel pumps rather than chargers.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the US dollar, and the price at which Africa's largest oil producer settles its imports. It carries fuel, food and freight costs into Nigerian shops, and it prices the government's foreign debt.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira firmed to its strongest of the month on 29 August, the day Moody's moved Nigeria's outlook to positive on stronger external buffers and foreign reserves hit a 20-year high. FTSE Russell will reclassify Nigeria from Unclassified on September 21, restoring frontier status. The buffers were built on the float and fuel-subsidy removal.

fx-egp.standing: The exchange rate of Egypt's currency against the US dollar. Egypt imports most of its wheat and fuel, so the pound's level sets the price of bread and energy for more than 100 million people and the cost of servicing state debt.
fx-egp.recent: The pound weakened after Washington cut off a major Egyptian bank from the global financial system on 28 August, part of a push by Bessent that also targeted banks in the UAE over Iran ties. The currency had reached 51.16 on 1 August and 49.56 on 8 August before settling near 50.26.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira's exchange rate against the US dollar. Turkey imports most of its energy and much of its food in dollars, so the rate sets domestic inflation, and a rising figure means each dollar buys more lira.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a fresh low across the month against a run of confrontations on Turkey's southern flank. Eight Israeli strikes hit an airbase in Syria's Idlib on 18 August, with Israel saying Syria's acceptance of Turkish troops posed a 'threat', and Ankara issued a genocide warrant for Netanyahu three days later.

fx-bdt.standing: The Bangladeshi taka against the US dollar. It sets the import bill for a country that buys its fuel, wheat and cotton abroad and pays for them in dollars, while its garment exports and worker remittances are what earn those dollars back.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka held in a narrow band, near 123 to the dollar, ranging only between 124 on Aug 7 and 122 on Aug 19. Nothing in the month's news — the election of Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as president, the confirmed purchase of Chinese J-10CE fighters — moved it beyond that range.

fx-idr.standing: The rupiah, Indonesia's currency, quoted as the number of rupiah one US dollar buys — so a rising number is a weakening currency. It prices the imports and dollar debt of Southeast Asia's largest economy, and moves on commodity earnings and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah is stronger than a month ago, off its Aug 4 low of 18,040 to 17,760. The month's news was mostly non-monetary: a quake in Sikka that killed 53 and cut Flores's coastal road, and Prabowo's widening state grip on the economy through cooperatives. Neither move in the currency traces cleanly to them.

fx-lbp.standing: The street price of Lebanon's currency against the dollar, the number most Lebanese households actually price life in. After the banking collapse wiped out savings, it is the clearest single reading of whether the state has stabilised anything.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has barely moved, drifting between 89,250 and 89,720 across the month — a peg holding while the country it belongs to does not. Israeli strikes have killed 4,350 people in Lebanon by the health ministry's count, three Christian villages near Ain Ebel remain inside an occupied border zone, and the currency registered none of it.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate of China's currency against the dollar, managed within a band the central bank sets each morning. It prices the world's largest exporter, so it feeds through to the cost of manufactured goods almost everywhere.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted stronger across the month, from 6.755 on Aug 4 to 6.721 on Aug 28, a move too small to point to any single cause. The backdrop is a currency doing steady work: Beijing tripled the number of banks issuing the digital yuan to 30, Nigeria took its oilfields to a Shandong trade fair to court Chinese capital, and Bangladesh confirmed a purchase of J-10CE jets.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the dollar. India imports most of its crude and gas, so a weaker rupee raises the cost of every barrel and cargo landed at its ports, and the pass-through reaches fuel pumps, freight and household bills.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee sat near the weak end of its month, touching 95.77 on Aug 20 before easing to 95.43. Indraprastha Gas raised Delhi CNG ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg, naming surging LNG prices after the West Asia escalation — the import bill a softer rupee makes heavier still.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker real. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, and its level sets the price of Brazil's imports and the dollar cost of its debt.
fx-brl.recent: The real weakened through the month, from 5.077 on Aug 3 to a high of 5.222 on Aug 15 and 5.194 now. The clearest domestic driver is the collapse of Bank Master in a fraud probe, Brazil's largest banking fraud case, which left the deposit-guarantee fund absorbing the loss.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate of Mexico's peso against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends the large majority of its exports to the United States, so the peso reacts fast to US trade policy and rate decisions.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso strengthened from 17.35 on Aug 1 to 16.92 by Aug 21 before easing to 17.03, a move of under two percent across the month. The input carries no Mexico-specific policy, trade or rate news that would explain the drift.

fx-eur.standing: The exchange rate between the euro and the US dollar, quoted here as euros per dollar. It is the most heavily traded currency pair in the world, and it sets the price of every import and export crossing between the two largest developed economies.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted lower across the month as Europe's confrontation with Russia widened. Berlin moved to attribute a bomb-rigged drone near a Leipzig cargo plane to Russia and prepare national sanctions, while the EU planned its broadest sanctions package yet and four member states pushed to unlock Russia's frozen billions.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate between Japan's currency and the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker yen. It is the world's main carry-trade funding currency, and a cheaper yen lifts Japanese exporters while raising the cost of the fuel and food the country imports.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen slid to 160.1 per dollar on 29 August, its weakest of the month against 156.5 on 3 August, as US long-dated borrowing costs climbed — thirty-year Treasury yields reached 5.3%, a 2007 level, widening the gap that pulls money out of yen. The dollar's softness against the euro on rate-hike bets did not carry over.

fx-rub.standing: Russia's currency, quoted as rubles per US dollar, so a higher number means a weaker ruble. It is priced under capital controls and sanctions rather than in a free global market, which makes it a running readout on how much hard currency the war economy can still earn.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble slid from 79.26 on Aug 1 to 86.15 on Aug 29 as the sanctions perimeter widened: Germany is preparing a national sanctions package over the bomb-rigged drone at Leipzig airport, and Washington's "Operation Economic Outcast" cut six Banque Misr branches off from US dollar access. At home, 4.2 trillion rubles are shifting into cash.

fx-zar.standing: The exchange rate of South Africa's currency against the US dollar. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, and its swings feed straight into South African fuel prices, import costs and the servicing burden on dollar debt.
fx-zar.recent: The rand firmed through August, reaching 15.92 on Aug 26 from a 16.56 high on Aug 1. Domestic news in the period was fiscal and political rather than market-moving: Pretoria's Treasury turning to R88.6bn in unclaimed dormant accounts and pensions, and the ANC's continued loss of voters. Nothing in the input explains the currency's move.

btc.standing: The first and largest cryptocurrency, traded around the clock against every major currency. It is priced on demand rather than earnings, which makes it a fast, noisy read on liquidity, dollar policy and appetite for risk.
btc.recent: The rally to $80,020 was a short squeeze rather than leveraged buying: $48 billion in futures open interest sat against $25 billion in daily volume, and the exit narrowed. Traders then priced Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, with Bitcoin up 21% on the week as the dollar repriced around one man's tone.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency by market value, and the settlement asset of a network that runs programmable contracts. Its price is a proxy for demand for on-chain finance itself, since most tokens, stablecoins and trading venues are built on it.
eth.recent: The rise came alongside a regulatory turn: the US securities regulator proposed a crypto rulebook on 23 August after scrapping an earlier Reg Crypto vote, and Andrew Cuomo pressed for the bill from Jackson Hole. In Seoul, Mirae's Park Hyeon-joo set a $109 billion target for a bank-owned exchange.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by an allocated bar of London Good Delivery gold, so its price tracks the metal itself. Gold is the asset people buy when they doubt a currency or a central bank, which is what makes it worth watching.
paxg.recent: Gold and bitcoin were both pricing Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, a test of Fed independence, and the metal peaked at 4,672 on Aug 25 in the days before it. Physical demand shows the same pull: in Kassala, street dealers now outbid the licensed market, and Sudanese gold leaks out at the official rate.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A Wikipedia article's daily readership is a rough gauge of public attention: how many people went looking for an explanation of the subject on a given day, rather than what was published about it.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: The mid-August peak came as the money behind AI drew scrutiny: Nvidia backstops $230 billion in customer lease obligations, Bullish is lending $100 million against GPUs that depreciate faster than the loan, and Alibaba raised $10 billion in new shares rather than spend cash on AI. Bill Gates then reversed his stance, saying AI will destroy far more jobs than he predicted in January.

wiki-russia.standing: The daily count of people reading the English Wikipedia article on Russia — a rough gauge of how many strangers to a subject are looking it up at once, and one that rises when a country stops being background and becomes the story.
wiki-russia.recent: The 17 August peak followed Ukraine's largest attack of the war a day earlier and the EU foreign affairs chief's push to expand sanctions against Russia. Readership stayed high through a missile strike that killed at least 13 in Kyiv on 20 August, and again on 29 August, when a strike on a warehouse near Kyiv killed at least 27 and Moscow claimed it had destroyed Ukraine's Flamingo missile plants.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, a country of some 240 million people whose politics, energy shortages and border tensions draw international attention in bursts rather than steadily.

wiki-china.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on China. It rises when the country is the subject of a story rather than the background to one, which makes it a rough gauge of where broad attention sits.
wiki-china.recent: The 13 August peak sits inside a run of stories placing China at the centre of other countries' decisions: Bangladesh confirming a deal for J-10CE fighters, Nigeria pitching Niger Delta oilfields at a Shandong trade fair as Western majors leave, and satellite imagery of new hangars at the Malan flight-test base. Flash floods on the Nepal-China border, which killed at least 160, drew a second wave of readers.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: A two-mile-wide shipping lane between Iran and Oman that carries roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil. There is no practical alternative route out of the Gulf, so whoever can close it holds a lever over the fuel supply of Asia and Europe.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Views tracked the strait's closure. The IRGC says Hormuz is shut to any vessel transiting without Iranian coordination, and the IMO counts 6,000 seafarers stranded aboard anchored ships inside the Gulf. Transits fell to a single gas carrier on one Monday; Iran and Oman have since opened a temporary corridor.

wiki-india.standing: The daily count of people opening Wikipedia's article on India. It is a rough gauge of global curiosity about the country — it climbs when something there reaches readers who do not follow it week to week.
wiki-india.recent: The 15 August peak fell on a run of India stories: a stampede at a temple in Bihar that killed 7 and injured 19, and US envoy Sergio Gor calling J&K an 'important part of India', which prompted Pakistan to summon the US envoy. Attention held through flash flooding on the Nepal-China border that killed at least 160 and left 288 Indians missing.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine, a proxy for how much of the world is looking up the country rather than scrolling past it. Attention concentrates on the days the war produces something people cannot place.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The 24 August peak came as Ukraine's allies convened in Kyiv and Zelenskyy said Patriot deliveries had halved since 2023, alongside Britain clearing MBDA to share SCALP component data with France and Ukraine. Attention held into the 29th, when a Russian strike on a warehouse in Bucha killed at least 27, most of them from secondary detonations of stored munitions.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic is running about half its 90-day baseline: 7 tankers crossed on Thursday, and Iran and Oman have opened only a temporary corridor rather than reopening the strait. The IRGC says nothing transits without its coordination and has tied terms to Gaza. Some 6,000 sailors remain stuck aboard anchored ships; Delhi's compressed natural gas rose ₹3.89 to ₹86.98 a kg.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic sits well below its own 90-day baseline after a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on 24 August, the latest in a run of attacks that also injured Pakistani nationals in the Red Sea. Saudi Arabia shelled villages in Yemen's Razih district the same day. Owners are routing around the strait rather than insure the passage.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic sits at 37 vessels a day, barely above its own 90-day baseline, with the Red Sea approach still unsafe: the Houthis said they attacked a vessel off Saudi Arabia on 24 August, and Pakistani nationals injured in an earlier Red Sea attack returned home. Cairo-brokered Gaza talks have not yet changed the route.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has run below its own 90-day baseline, thinning from the June peak with no weather behind it — waves have stayed near flat. The pressure has been upstream: shipping in Hormuz has slowed to a near halt, and Houthi missiles hit a Saudi tanker off Yanbu, cutting the volume of tankers that reach Malacca at all.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic sits near its 90-day baseline, down 3.3% over the last week, with no weather alert and waves under 1.1m. Nothing in the record explains the swing between the 10 July low of 28 vessels and the 12 July peak of 401.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: The canal is capping daily transits in anticipation of a severe El Niño, the drought pattern that drains the lakes its locks depend on; traffic is running about a fifth below its own 90-day baseline, at 28 vessels a day against a 83-vessel peak on Jul 13. CK Hutchison is separately seeking HK$11.7b from Panama over a canal ports dispute.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has thinned as the Black Sea itself became dangerous: a third Greek vessel in three days burned there on 18 August, and daily transits bottomed at 38 on 16 August against a 9 June high of 100. Turkey's naval attention has been elsewhere too, with a ten-day operation off Somalia that killed 14 pirates.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic has run about 5.6% below its 90-day baseline, with the 84-day range bounded by 112 vessels on 3 June and 163 on 13 June. The input does not identify a cause for the shortfall.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic through the strait is running about 6% below its 90-day baseline, with rough seas and waves near 2.9 metres over the latest window — conditions that slow crossings and hold ferries and smaller vessels in port. The coverage in this period does not otherwise explain the decline.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic sits near its 90-day baseline despite continued attacks on shipping: a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on 24 August, and traffic through Hormuz slowed to a near halt in mid-August as a 60-day deadline for a US-Iran MoU expired. Rough seas, with waves to 2.9m, met the vessels rounding the cape.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to nothing — no vessels recorded since the strait last cleared 25 in early June, and the past week runs 97% below its own 90-day baseline. The strait sits inside a war the Kremlin has escalated rather than settled: sources in Moscow declared the peace talks dead, Russia struck nine cities in one night, and early voting opened in occupied Ukrainian territory.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index reached its 36-day high of 11,260 on 26 August, the same week Washington sent the Saudi nuclear deal to Congress — a text that skips an enrichment ban and awaits Saudi recognition of Israel. Riyadh also signed a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Turkey in Mecca, and shelled villages in Yemen's Razih district.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index recovered from its Jul 30 low of 13,290 to 14,640 through a month in which Turkey's regional exposure widened rather than eased: eight Israeli strikes hit an airbase in Syria's Idlib on 18 August, with Israel saying Syria's acceptance of Turkish troops posed a 'threat', and Ankara issued a genocide warrant for Netanyahu three days later.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index fell after Iran fired two ballistic missiles at the UAE on 18 August, triggering Dubai's first emergency alert in months, and the UAE responded by suspending all trade and financial transactions with Iran. Pressure continued on 28 August as Bessent targeted banks in the UAE over Iran ties.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index reached its 65-day high on Aug 26 before slipping, with the political calendar the visible event: prosecutors charged former prime minister Ismail Sabri with concealing assets, alleging $40 million hidden, on Aug 27. The index closed at 1726, still up over the period from its Jul 1 low of 1657.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index climbed through August as Prabowo's government tightened its grip on the economy, running more of it through cooperatives and state channels — a shift domestic investors have priced as directed spending rather than risk. It reached 6526 on Aug 21, up a fifth from its Jun 8 low of 5342.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The index sits near the middle of its 65-day range, between a 72,370 high on Jun 25 and a 61,430 low on Jul 29, and the input does not explain the swing. The clearest business news in the window is India's trade push: Piyush Goyal brought 200 firms to Tokyo, with the two countries set to review their trade pact and streamline investment.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after recovering from a late-June low, with mainland-facing trade and policy the dominant inputs. Wang Yi told Washington to "remove disruptions" ahead of a summit, while Chinese EV makers absorbed EU tariffs rather than passing them on.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index has drifted down roughly 4% since late June, and the input names no domestic driver for the slide. What Chinese firms did over the window sits abroad: Nigeria pitching oilfields at a Shandong trade fair, a confirmed J-10CE sale to Bangladesh, and EV exports absorbing EU tariffs.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index has fallen roughly a fifth over the window, with the Bank of Korea hiking rates to 3.00% on 27 August in consecutive increases the central bank framed as prioritising financial stability. SK Hynix said it was weighing closer ties with Kioxia, and Washington scrapped next month's Twin Dragons exercise.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index has drifted up over the window, peaking on Aug 6 before easing, and the Mumbai news since has been corporate rather than macro: HDFC Bank's chief executive declined a third term, leaving succession at India's largest private lender open. Nothing in the record explains the move itself.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed 13.93% over the past 64 days to a high of 5768 on Aug 17, with Singapore's role as a regional financial hub in evidence: crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion, and a 70-member Indian delegation arrived on Aug 19 for talks on tech, investment and trade ties.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after recovering from a low on Jul 30. Two things weigh on it from opposite directions: Taiwan indicted nine people, including an Nvidia manager, over AI server smuggling on 24 August, and Xiaomi's Xring O3 chip arrived the same day as a direct challenge to Qualcomm.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index climbed about 5.5% over the past five weeks, reaching 1,639 on Jul 17 after a low of 1,541 on Jun 23. Nothing in the recent Thai news flow — a deputy PM's push for cybersecurity cooperation with Russia, the murder of Russian tourists in Pattaya — accounts for the move.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits at its 37-day high after a 7.4% run from its late-May low, and the political news out of Manila has not dented it: an ex-disbursing officer told the Senate impeachment court that Duterte ordered a P125-million confidential funds transfer. Nothing in that testimony touches the listed companies the index tracks.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a run from May, though it slipped on the last session. The move down came ahead of inflation data, the release traders had been positioned for. Corporate news was thin: KPMG Australia cut 27 partners and 360 staff, about 5% of its workforce.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index climbed to 118,200 on Aug 28, its highest of the period and up from 108,300 on Jul 23. The domestic news in this window was fiscal and social rather than corporate: Treasury moving on R88.6bn in unclaimed dormant accounts and pensions, and Ghana declining an MTN donation. Neither explains the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index sagged to its low on 18 August as Brazil's Bank Master collapsed in a fraud probe, a supervisory failure that left depositors and the deposit-guarantee fund carrying the loss. It has since recovered most of the ground, closing near 175,700, helped by Petrobras detecting signs of oil off the Amazon coast — the frontier prospect Lula called a "passport.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index has drifted down about 5% over the past three months, from its Jun 2 high of 68,890 to a low of 63,930 on Aug 18, and sits near 65,480. Nothing in the available material explains the decline.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index has drifted down about 3% over the past three months, off its 22 July high of 3,380,000 and near the 19 August low of 2,874,000. The one Buenos Aires story in the window is an Interpol operation that dismantled a fraud network, with 58 arrested and 196 identified — nothing that explains the move in equities.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index held near its high through the breakdown of Canada-US trade talks: Washington imposed new tariffs on 22 August, Ottawa answered dollar for dollar with a list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles, and Ontario Premier Doug Ford threatened to cut power exports. Energy and mining weightings absorbed the shock.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index sits near its 13 August high after drifting through late August, and the input offers no market-moving cause for the move. The period's larger US business news was Meta's $16.68B settlement over social media harms to children, and Washington's "Operation Economic Outcast" sanctions campaign aimed at isolating Iran's economy.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index has drifted up about 3.8% over the window, reaching 10,910 on Jul 29 before easing, with no single event in view to explain the move.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index climbed to a series high of 26570 on Aug 28, up 5.9% over the window, as Berlin moved towards sanctioning Russia over the Leipzig airport drone attack and Brussels prepared what Kallas calls the broadest package yet. Sanctions-exposed firms are the ones carrying that risk.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Paris equities sit near the top of a 67-day range, having climbed from a June low to a 10 August peak before easing back. The coverage window is dominated by European space policy rather than market news — the European Space Agency's €544 million award to three rocket startups, and its plan to adapt Ariane 6 for nuclear-powered Argonaut landers — none of which explains the index move.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index has climbed about 7% over the window, reaching its high on Aug 13 and holding near it since. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index has climbed nearly 9% over the window, reaching 20,210 on Aug 11 before easing to 19,880. Nothing in the available reporting explains the move.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, up about five percent over the window, with the high on Aug 7 and a fall of just over one percent on the latest day. The input carries no Milan-specific event that explains the move.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, up about 6.6% over the period, having climbed from a low of 13,220 on Jun 3 to a high of 14,630 on Aug 10 before easing to 14,400. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index closed at its 66-day high on 28 August, up about 7 percent from its 10 June low. Nothing in the available material explains the climb.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at the next meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves as the case for a cut or a hike is made and unmade.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The contract sat at 39% on Aug 1 and reached 75% on Aug 15, a hold looking close to settled before it fell back to 51%. Fed minutes released Aug 19 showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, which bitcoin and gold were already pricing, put the question back open.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia biography of the sitting US president, and one of the most-read pages on the site. Daily readership rises and falls with what the office does, making it a rough gauge of how far a decision has travelled beyond the people it directly affects.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The 26 August peak came as Washington's Saudi nuclear deal was reported to skip an enrichment ban and to await Saudi recognition of Israel, alongside a widened sanctions push on Iran that Tehran vowed to resist. Readership had climbed from its 15 August low through Kushner's Gaza talks with Hamas and Netanyahu.

wiki-stablecoin.standing: A crypto token pegged to a national currency, usually the dollar, and backed by reserves held off-chain. It is the settlement layer for most crypto trading, and increasingly a payment rail that moves value without touching a bank's books.
wiki-stablecoin.recent: Banks moved onto the rail rather than against it: Shinhan began building won stablecoin rails with a card network, Standard Chartered started distributing Hong Kong's dollar stablecoin, and crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion. In Washington, 39 state banking associations announced a rival chain to defend deposits.

wiki-united-states.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on the United States each day. A country's main encyclopedia page is where readers go first when a place makes news, so the count tracks attention rather than events.
wiki-united-states.recent: Courts moved against the administration on several fronts at once around the Aug 28 peak: Judge Noel Wise struck down Rubio's visa policy, Judge Rita Lin vacated the Anthropic ban, and Postal Service mail-ballot rules were blocked for 14 days. The US had unveiled "Operation Economic Outcast" against Iran that Monday.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: Wikipedia readership for Bitcoin, the first cryptocurrency and the one whose price and plumbing set the terms for the rest. Attention here tracks when the asset stops being a market story and becomes a general one.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: The 24 August peak sat between two stories: a rally to $80,020, up 23.7% in a week, that turned out to be a short squeeze rather than fresh leverage, and Rakbank Islamic opening Bitcoin trading inside a shariah-compliant platform after its board cleared it. Reading has drifted down since.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington and Tehran hold a ceasefire by a set date. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on each escalation and each opening — a strait, a sanction, a back channel.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: The rise came as the pressure shifted from missiles to money: Washington unveiled "Operation Economic Outcast" and cut six Banque Misr branches out of dollar clearing, and Pezeshkian conceded foreign trade has shrunk by more than a third. Hormuz was declared open on 28 Aug after Iran and Oman charted a temporary corridor.

wiki-nepal.standing: Wikipedia's daily readership for the country's own article, a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking Nepal up on any given day. It sits flat for months and then jumps when the country reaches a global audience.
wiki-nepal.recent: A flash flood tore down the Nepal–Tibet border valleys on 26 August without rain falling first, killing at least 160 and leaving hundreds missing, and readership climbed with the search. The peak on 27 August came as a barrier lake holding 2 million cubic metres formed behind a landslide dam and 934 workers were counted trapped or missing across eleven hydropower sites.

fed-funds.standing: The interest rate the US Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between banks. It is the base cost of dollar credit, and mortgages, corporate borrowing and the price of the dollar abroad all take their cue from it.
fed-funds.recent: The rate has been held at 3.75% since December 2025, down from 5.5% in August 2024, but the direction of travel has reversed: Fed minutes released on 19 August showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and markets now favor a September hike. Attention has centred on Warsh's Jackson Hole speech.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays commercial banks to park cash overnight, and the floor under euro-zone borrowing costs. It sets what savers earn and what mortgages, business loans and government debt cost across the currency bloc.
ecb-rate.recent: The rate sits at 2.25%, down from 3.75% in Aug 2024 and a quarter-point above the Jun 2025 low of 2%, and the input does not explain the latest move. Elsewhere the direction has turned: the Bank of Korea hiked to 3.00%, and Fed minutes showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force that is looking for work and cannot find it, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the number the Federal Reserve weighs against inflation when it sets interest rates.
us-unemployment.recent: The rate stands at 4.1%, down from the 4.5% high reached in November 2025 and close to the 4% low of January 2025. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Marco Rubio becomes the Republican nominee for president in 2028. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on primary field news, endorsements and anything that reshapes the party's next contest.
poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.recent: The contract slid from 28 on Jul 31 to 17 on Aug 28, with nothing in the prediction-market news explaining the nomination itself: the stories in the window are about the venues rather than the race. A White House aide paid a fine over bets on the president's speeches, and the Ninth Circuit ruled that sports bets aren't "swaps," curbing Kalshi.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Bab el-Mandeb Strait — the 20-mile gate between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden — is effectively closed to shipping. It is a bet on the route that carries Suez-bound trade between Europe and Asia.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: The price fell from 16% on Aug 1 to 5% on Aug 30, traders steadily discounting a closure. Polymarket itself has been under pressure over the period: South Korea joined more than 30 jurisdictions restricting access on Aug 18, and 152 wallets were found to hold a 97.2% win rate on war-related contracts.

poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Édouard Philippe, the former prime minister who now leads his own centre-right party, wins the French presidency in 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.
poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.recent: The contract has barely moved. It has held a one-point band for the whole 32-day window: 26% at the high on 31 July, 25% at the low on 24 August, and 26% now. Nothing in that month repriced it.

wiki-nigeria.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Nigeria — Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer. Readership rises when the country's politics, security or economy reach an international audience.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Attention drifted down through August after an early-month peak, with the news arriving late: Moody's moved Nigeria's outlook to positive on stronger external buffers as reserves hit a 20-year high, and FTSE Russell said it will reclassify Nigeria from Unclassified on September 21. Atiku Abubakar's pledge to restore the petrol subsidy in 2027 ran across 32 outlets.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on candidacy decisions, court rulings and polling rather than on any single campaign event.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: The contract has climbed from 24% on Jul 31 to 40% on Aug 30, a two-thirds rise over the month. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-us-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Kamala Harris wins the 2028 US presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with candidate news rather than with any poll.
poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-us-.recent: The contract has drifted down across the month, from 5% on Jul 31 to a low of 3% on Aug 25 and 4% now, with no Harris news behind it. What moved in this market was its plumbing: the Ninth Circuit ruled Kalshi's sports bets aren't "swaps," and a White House aide was fined for betting on speeches he read early.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington declares its naval blockade of Iran over by a set date. It prices how long traders think the cordon holds, and the answer sets insurance, freight and oil-supply expectations across the Gulf.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: The odds fell from 96 on Aug 6 to 62 as the blockade hardened rather than lifted. Washington unveiled "Operation Economic Outcast" and cut six Banque Misr branches out of dollar clearing, Tehran said foreign trade has shrunk by more than a third, and the IRGC claimed a veto over Hormuz even after Trump declared the strait clear.

poly-will-jon-ossoff-win-the-2028-democr.standing: A Polymarket contract on Jon Ossoff's chances in the 2028 Democratic race, priced in cents on the dollar. It is what traders will pay for the outcome, not a poll, and it reprices the moment money changes hands.
poly-will-jon-ossoff-win-the-2028-democr.recent: The contract has held a narrow band for the month: 13% on Jul 31, a high of 17% on Aug 6, and 16% now.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran loses control of Kharg Island, the terminal that loads most of its crude for export. Traders price it as a proxy for how far a war against Iran's economy is expected to go beyond sanctions and blockade.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: The odds fell from 14% on Aug 1 to 6% on Aug 29 as the pressure on Iran stayed financial rather than territorial: Washington's "Operation Economic Outcast" cut six Banque Misr branches out of dollar clearing, and Pezeshkian conceded foreign trade has shrunk by more than a third. Hormuz reopened partially under an Iran-Oman corridor.

wiki-israel.standing: The Wikipedia article on Israel, and the daily count of people who open it. Readership of a country page is a rough gauge of how many people outside a story are trying to orient themselves in it.
wiki-israel.recent: The 25 August peak of 32,400 views came as Israeli armoured vehicles expelled 20 UN refugee-agency staff from the Qalandia camp campus and Lebanon reported glyphosate at 50 times normal levels in the soil at Ayta ash-Shaab. Readership has since fallen back to 11,700, near the 8 August low, even as strikes continued inside the ceasefire.

poly-will-anthropic-have-the-best-ai-mod.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Anthropic will be judged to have the strongest AI model when the year closes. It prices a race between a handful of frontier labs, and traders reprice it every time one of them ships.
poly-will-anthropic-have-the-best-ai-mod.recent: The contract climbed from 78 on Aug 11 to 94, its high, on Aug 30. Nothing in the window explains the move directly; the Polymarket news of the period concerned the venue rather than this market, including South Korea joining more than 30 jurisdictions restricting Polymarket access.

poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve holds its policy rate flat through the whole of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves whenever the case for easing strengthens or weakens.
poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.recent: The market has held near the top of its range all month, and Fed minutes released on 19 August pointed the other way from cuts entirely, with many officials saying rate hikes may be needed. The dip to 85 on 9 August did not last. Attention around Polymarket itself has been legal rather than monetary: the Ninth Circuit ruled against Kalshi on 28 August, and a White House aide was fined for betting on presidential speeches.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-finis.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Lula finishes second in Brazil's presidential race, priced as a percentage that traders will pay for that outcome. It is a bet on the shape of the field, not just on who wins.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-finis.recent: The contract has risen from 5% on Aug 5 to 13% on Aug 30, and the input does not carry Brazilian election news that explains the move.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the party that has held a governing majority in Russia's State Duma for two decades, takes the most seats at the next legislative election. Traders price it as a bet, not a forecast.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: The odds climbed from 60 on Jul 31 to 75 on Aug 30 as the war hardened rather than wound down: Kremlin sources declared the peace talks dead, Russia claimed it destroyed Ukraine's Flamingo missile plants, and four EU states pushed to unlock Russia's frozen billions. Zelenskyy separately rejected a wartime vote in Ukraine.

xag.standing: A token tracking the price of an ounce of silver, held against allocated bullion. Silver is both a monetary metal bought as a store of value and an industrial input, used in solar cells, electrical contacts and electronics.
xag.recent: The series more than doubled off its 6 August low of $29.81, reaching $69.42 on 28 August before easing to $66.31. The input carries no supply, policy or demand event that accounts for a move of that size.
